steps.title: Import Component, ErrorHandler, Injectable, and NgModule from Angular core
steps.instruction: Import Component, ErrorHandler, Injectable, and NgModule from '@angular/core'.
steps.hint: Use the import statement with curly braces to import multiple symbols from the Angular core module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing multiple Angular core modules
import { Component, Injectable } from '@angular/core';
steps.seedCode: // Import Component, ErrorHandler, Injectable, and NgModule from '@angular/core'
steps.expectedOutcome: The Angular core modules needed for error handling are imported.
successCriteria: Component, ErrorHandler, Injectable, and NgModule are imported from '@angular/core'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported the required Angular core modules for error handling.
steps.feedbackPartial: You imported some modules, but make sure to include all four: Component, ErrorHandler, Injectable, and NgModule.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are missing or incorrect. Please import Component, ErrorHandler, Injectable, and NgModule from '@angular/core'.

steps.title: Create a custom ErrorHandler service
steps.instruction: Create a new service class named 'CustomErrorHandler' that extends Angular's built-in ErrorHandler and mark it as Injectable.
steps.hint: Use the @Injectable() decorator above your class definition and make sure it extends ErrorHandler.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a CustomErrorHandler service class ready to implement custom error handling logic.
successCriteria: The CustomErrorHandler class exists, extends ErrorHandler, and is decorated with @Injectable().
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a custom error handler service that extends Angular's built-in ErrorHandler.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your class extends ErrorHandler and has the @Injectable() decorator.
steps.feedbackWrong: The service class isn't properly defined. Remember to create a class named CustomErrorHandler that extends ErrorHandler and add the @Injectable() decorator.

steps.title: Override the handleError method
steps.instruction: Inside your CustomErrorHandler class, override the handleError method to log the error to the console with a custom message.
steps.hint: Use the override keyword before the method name and implement the method body to call console.error with your message.
steps.expectedOutcome: The CustomErrorHandler class will have a handleError method that logs errors with a custom message.
successCriteria: The handleError method is overridden with the override keyword and contains console.error with a custom message.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully overridden the handleError method. This is where you'll implement your custom error handling logic.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using the override keyword and implementing the method body to log the error.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleError method needs to be overridden with the override keyword and should log errors to the console.

steps.title: Create a component that will throw an error
steps.instruction: Create a new Angular component named 'ErrorThrowingComponent' with a simple template containing a button and a method that throws an error when the button is clicked.
steps.hint: Use the @Component decorator to define the component. Add a button in the template with a click event that calls a method. In that method, throw a new Error.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a new component that can be used to simulate an error condition in your application.
successCriteria: The ErrorThrowingComponent is created with a @Component decorator, contains a button in its template, and has a method that throws an error when the button is clicked.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a component that simulates an error condition. This will help demonstrate how error boundaries work.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your component has both a template with a button and a method that throws an error when that button is clicked.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component doesn't seem to be set up correctly. Remember to use @Component decorator, include a button in the template, and create a method that throws an error.

steps.title: Add a button to trigger the error
steps.instruction: In the ErrorThrowingComponent's template, add a button with the text 'Throw Error' that calls a method named throwError when clicked.
steps.hint: Use the (click) event binding to call the throwError method. The button should be inside the component's template.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template now includes a button that will trigger an error when clicked.
successCriteria: The ErrorThrowingComponent has a button with (click)="throwError()" and the text 'Throw Error' in its template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a button that will trigger an error when clicked.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the button has the correct text and the (click) event binding calls throwError().
steps.feedbackWrong: The button is missing or not properly configured. Check the template for the button with (click)="throwError()".

steps.title: Register the custom ErrorHandler in the module
steps.instruction: Add your CustomErrorHandler service to the providers array of the NgModule.
steps.hint: In the NgModule decorator, include providers: [CustomErrorHandler] to replace Angular's default error handler.
steps.expectedOutcome: The NgModule will be configured to use your custom error handler service instead of Angular's default.
successCriteria: CustomErrorHandler is listed in the providers array of the NgModule decorator.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully registered your custom error handler. Angular will now use it to handle errors.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure CustomErrorHandler is added to the providers array inside the NgModule decorator.
steps.feedbackWrong: The custom error handler isn't registered yet. Add CustomErrorHandler to the providers array in the NgModule.

steps.title: Add error state to the component
steps.instruction: In the ErrorThrowingComponent class, add a boolean property named 'hasError' to track whether an error has occurred.
steps.hint: Add a property with type boolean and initialize it to false in the component class.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ErrorThrowingComponent will have a boolean property 'hasError' initialized to false, ready to track error conditions.
successCriteria: The ErrorThrowingComponent class contains a boolean property named 'hasError' initialized to false.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the error state property. This will allow the component to track when an error occurs.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added a boolean property named 'hasError' with an initial value of false in the ErrorThrowingComponent class.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component doesn't have the required error state property. Add a boolean property named 'hasError' initialized to false in the ErrorThrowingComponent class.

steps.title: Update the error handler to set the error state
steps.instruction: In the CustomErrorHandler class, modify the handleError method to update the ErrorThrowingComponent's hasError property to true when an error occurs.
steps.hint: You'll need to access the ErrorThrowingComponent instance. Consider how you might pass component state to the error handler.
steps.expectedOutcome: The handleError method now updates the component's error state when an error is caught.
successCriteria: The CustomErrorHandler's handleError method sets the ErrorThrowingComponent's hasError property to true.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully connected the error handler to update the component's error state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the handleError method explicitly sets the component's hasError property to true.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleError method should update the component's error state. Review how to access and modify component properties from the error handler.

steps.title: Add conditional rendering based on error state
steps.instruction: In the ErrorThrowingComponent template, use *ngIf to show an error message when hasError is true, and keep the button visible only when hasError is false.
steps.hint: You can use two separate *ngIf directives: one for the error message and one for the button. The error message should display when hasError is true.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template now includes conditional rendering that displays an error message when an error occurs and hides the button, showing the button only when no error is present.
successCriteria: The template contains *ngIf directives that conditionally show an error message when hasError is true and the button when hasError is false.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added conditional rendering to show different content based on the error state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have both *ngIf conditions: one for the error message and one for the button.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't yet have the conditional rendering. Remember to use *ngIf to show the error message when hasError is true and the button when hasError is false.

steps.title: Add a reset mechanism to recover from errors
steps.instruction: Add a reset button to the ErrorThrowingComponent template that clears the error state when clicked.
steps.hint: Add a button element next to the existing button in the template, and bind its click event to a method that sets hasError back to false.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template will have a second button labeled 'Reset' that, when clicked, will clear the error state.
successCriteria: A reset button is added to the template with a click handler that sets hasError to false.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a reset mechanism to recover from errors.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a reset button, but make sure it properly clears the error state when clicked.
steps.feedbackWrong: The reset button or its functionality is missing. Add a button that clears the error state.
